intro.text: **Built for live conversations.** Pick who you're talking to, then go to **🗡️ Offense** (you bring the case) or **🛡️ Defense** (they raised an objection).

**How to use the links:** every ▶ link jumps to a live conversation where the move is demonstrated. Lines tagged **➕** are supplemental material. Double-check those before leaning on them.
Doctrinal frame: historic Reformed orthodoxy (WCF / 1689). One Being, three Persons; Christ has two natures; Scripture alone.
What wins informal conversations isn't knowing more verses. It's **how you run the conversation**. Use these moves every time.

moves.title: Phase 1 = agree on the plain text. Nothing else moves until they do.
moves.text: He reads the verse and asks a yes/no question about what it *says* (not what it means). He won't go on until they answer. *"I'm not moving to Phase 2 until you answer Phase 1."*

moves.title: Yes/no questions, one at a time.
moves.text: *"Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?"* Short questions are hard to wriggle out of. Long statements give them room to filibuster.

moves.title: Call out the dodge out loud.
moves.text: When they redefine a word ("personification," "communicates information," "a vibe"), he names it: *"I didn't ask about personification. I asked, can He speak?"*

moves.title: Use their rule on another verse.
moves.text: When they invent a rule for one verse (e.g. "no article = 'a god'"), apply the same rule somewhere it obviously fails (John 1:6 becomes "a man sent from *a god* named *a John*").

moves.title: Hold them to their own analogy.
moves.text: If they bring an analogy (king and messenger, software coder, three judges), don't swap it out. Push it until it proves your point: *"Can the agent of the king claim to BE the king?"*

moves.title: No topic-hopping.
moves.text: When they're losing, they'll jump to "Is Jesus God?" or "the Trinity makes no sense." Don't follow. *"You're not going to 'is Jesus God' your way out of this. Defend your claim first."*

moves.title: Name the goalpost shift.
moves.text: *"First you wanted a Bible verse. I gave you the verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' own mouth?"*

moves.title: "What's the only thing we do? Read."
moves.text: When they say "context," make *them* show the verse in the context. Then wait. Silence works for you.

moves.title: Ask the question back.
moves.text: End with a question they have to answer on their own (*"Who is the Father hearing from?"*), not a speech.

moves.title: Stay warm.
moves.text: Even when they rage-quit: *"I want you to be saved, brother. I love you."* Truth with love keeps the door open (1 Pet 3:15–16).

universalTools.title: "Yahweh" isn't one-person-only.
universalTools.text: "Yahweh" can name the one divine nature, or any one of the Persons. Their "then Jesus is his own Father" syllogism only works if Yahweh = the Father alone. Show them "Judah" can mean a man *or* a tribe (Judges 1:1–2).

universalTools.title: Word–concept fallacy.
universalTools.text: "'Trinity' isn't in the Bible" → neither are "monotheism" or "Bible." The question is whether the *concept* is there.

universalTools.title: Three in one way, one in another.
universalTools.text: Not a contradiction. Different categories: 3 *persons*, 1 *being*. (For Muslims, hold up the Hafs, Warsh and Qalun Qurans.)

universalTools.title: Context decides literal vs. figurative.
universalTools.text: Both sides agree personification exists. But personified things don't say "set apart for **me**" or "the work **I** have called them to."

universalTools.title: "Firstborn" = rank, not birth order.
universalTools.text: David was the *youngest* son and the *second* king, yet God calls him "firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth" (Ps 89:27).

holySpiritPlay.title: 🔥 THE HOLY SPIRIT PLAY: "the Spirit is Yahweh" (Unitarians, JWs, Oneness, Muslims)

intro.text: **Why this is the kill shot:** Unitarians spend all their energy on Jesus (agency, *shaliach*, "a god"). They usually have **no prepared answer for the Spirit**. *"Holy Spirit: kryptonite for these guys."* Two steps: **(A) the Spirit is a Person → (B) that Person is Yahweh.**

stepA.title: Step A: The Spirit is a *Who*, not a *what*

opener.text: *"Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?"*

rows.point: "Set apart for **me** Barnabas and Saul for the work to which **I** have called them." First-person speech, a choice, authority.
rows.question: *"Do actions have authority, or do persons?"* / *"He said 'I' and 'me' about Himself. That's self-awareness, right?"*

rows.point: "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit **and to us**." He takes part in a decision alongside the apostles.
rows.question: *"Can a force agree with a council?"*

rows.point: He can be grieved and rebelled against.
rows.question: *"An active force can't be offended. Whoever the Spirit is, He's someone you **can** offend."*

rows.point: He "does not speak on His own; whatever He **hears** He speaks."
rows.question: (vs. Oneness or "Spirit = the Father") *"Who is the Father hearing from?"*
*"Christ is called God's power and He's a person. So being God's power doesn't rule out being a person, right?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"That's personification."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"I didn't ask about figurative language. Can He speak, yes or no? If I say 'my car told me it's not starting today,' did my car speak?"*. Then: personified wisdom never chooses missionaries in real time (Acts 13:2).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He just communicates information / He has no mouth."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"Does the Father have a mouth? Does the Father speak?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The Father told the Spirit to say it."*
ifTheySay.youSay: The text says "for **me**… **I** have called." That's not quoting someone else.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He's rational energy, like AI."*
ifTheySay.youSay: AI is programmed. The Spirit wills, commands and is provoked. *"Can energy be rational without personhood?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"God used the Spirit's power to create."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God also created *through Christ* (John 1:3), and Christ is a person.

stepB.title: Step B: That Person is Yahweh

structure.text: an OT text says **Yahweh** spoke → the NT says **the Holy Spirit** said it.

rows.first: **2 Sam 23:2–3**: "The **Spirit of Yahweh** speaks by me… the God of Israel has said"
rows.second: **Acts 4:24–25**: the "Sovereign Lord… who **by the Holy Spirit**, through the mouth of David"
rows.note: Go-to question: *"So the Sovereign Lord who spoke through David is who?"*

rows.first: **Ps 95:7–11**: "They tested **Me**… I swore in **My** wrath" (Yahweh speaking)
rows.second: **Heb 3:7–11**: "As **the Holy Spirit says**… they tested **Me**… I swore in **My** wrath"
rows.note: *"Who is the Spirit talking about when He says 'they provoked **Me**'?"*

rows.first: ➕ **Isa 6:8–10**: the voice of **the Lord** (Yahweh of hosts, v.3–5) says "Go, and say to this people…"
rows.second: ➕ **Acts 28:25–26**: "**The Holy Spirit** was right in saying to your fathers through Isaiah, 'Go to this people…'"
rows.note: Also John 12:41: Isaiah saw *Christ's* glory. One vision, three Persons.

rows.first: ➕ **Jer 31:31–34**: "This is the covenant **I** will make… **declares Yahweh**"
rows.second: ➕ **Heb 10:15–17**: "**The Holy Spirit** also bears witness… 'This is the covenant **I** will make'"
rows.note: The Spirit speaks Yahweh's covenant in the first person.

rows.first: ➕ **Acts 5:3–4**: "lie to **the Holy Spirit**" = "you have not lied to men but to **God**"

rows.second: The Spirit is the "Spirit of God" **and** the "Spirit of Christ"
rows.note: If the Spirit is Yahweh's own Spirit and also Christ's…

otOnly.label: Old Testament only (when they say "no NT")
otOnly.text: Deut 6:4 → Gen 1:2 (the Spirit of God) → 2 Sam 23:2–3 → Gen 31:11–13 / 35:1 (the Angel = the God of Bethel. *"Why is God saying 'go meet the God you met'?"*) → Zech 12:10 (*"they will look on **Me** whom they pierced." "Who did they pierce?"*). *"I don't need the New Testament to prove the Trinity."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The 'Spirit of Yahweh' means 'from Yahweh,' not 'is Yahweh.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"The answer is yes to all of them."* From Yahweh, and also Yahweh. Not either/or. Then: *"He's also the Spirit of Christ, right?"* (Rom 8:9). If they deny it, read the verse.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"OK, so the Spirit is just the Father."*
ifTheySay.youSay: John 16:13 (He hears from another), John 14:16 (*another* Helper whom the Father sends). *"Then the Father sends Himself and listens to Himself?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: They admit it but leave the Bible (an ex-JW who became Muslim because "the Bible says the Spirit is God")
ifTheySay.youSay: that's 2 Tim 4:3, "itching ears." He's conceding the Bible teaches it.

closer.text: *"You've agreed the Spirit speaks, chooses, and is grieved, so He's a who. And Scripture says that Who is Yahweh. So Yahweh is more than one Person. Now let's talk about the Son."*

beliefs.text: Jehovah = the Father only. Jesus = Michael the Archangel, Jehovah's first creation, "a god." The Holy Spirit = God's impersonal "active force." The NWT is the authoritative translation; the Watchtower (Governing Body) is the "faithful and discreet slave."

lead.label: Get this first
lead.text: *"If the Bible disagrees with the Watchtower, you'd side with the Bible, right?"* Lock in that commitment before you open a verse.

cheatCard.text: **John 1:3**: "*not one thing* came into existence without Him" → *"So did Jesus create Himself?"*
**Col 1:16–17 (NWT)**: "all *other* things." The word "other" isn't in the Greek, and the Watchtower's own interlinear shows it.
**Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17 / 22:13**: First and Last → *"Does being the First and Last mean you have a beginning?"*
**Heb 1:10–12 + Ps 102:25–27**: the Father addresses the Son with a Psalm spoken *to Jehovah* as Creator.
**Acts 13:2 + Heb 3:7–11**: the Spirit says "me / I," and the Spirit is the one tested in the wilderness → see [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play).
**Deut 18:21–22**: the 1914 / 1925 predictions → the test of a prophet.

chain.text: **John 1:3**: "All things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence." *"Does it say 'except himself'?"*
*"If not one thing came into existence without Him, and Jesus came into existence, then Jehovah used Jesus to make Jesus?"* *"That dog won't hunt."*
**Col 1:16–17 (NWT)**: point out "all *other* things," four times. *"Where is 'other' in the Greek?"* It's *ta panta*, "all things." The Watchtower's **own Kingdom Interlinear** has no "other."

➕ **Isa 44:24**: "I, Jehovah… stretched out the heavens **by myself**, who spread out the earth. **Who was with me?**" → *"If Jehovah created alone, and all things were created through Jesus, who is Jesus?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"'All' doesn't always mean all."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Here the verse defines it: "in the heavens and on the earth, visible and invisible, thrones, lordships" (Col 1:16). And John 1:3 says "not **one** thing."

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He was Jehovah's master worker (Prov 8:30)."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Working alongside doesn't mean created. And Prov 8 personifies Wisdom (a "she"). Is God ever without wisdom?

opener.text: *"According to John 1:3, how many things came into existence without the Word?"* (Answer: not one.)

closer.text: *"Everything that has ever come into existence came through Jesus. So Jesus has always existed. Do you agree?"*

chain.text: **Isa 44:6; 48:12**: Jehovah is "the first and the last; besides me there is no God."
**Rev 1:17–18**: "I am the First and the Last… I **became dead**." *"When did Jehovah die?"* So the speaker is Jesus.
**Rev 22:13, 16**: "Alpha and Omega, First and Last… I, **Jesus**." *"So Jesus has a beginning, but Jehovah doesn't, with the same title?"*

**Heb 1:8, 10–12**: the Father says to the Son, "You, Lord, in the beginning laid the foundation of the earth" — quoting **Ps 102:25–27**, which is addressed *to Jehovah*. *"Who is the Psalm talking to? And who does Hebrews apply it to?"*
➕ **Isa 45:23 → Phil 2:10–11**: "To **me** every knee will bow" (Yahweh) → "at the name of **Jesus** every knee should bow."
➕ **Isa 6:1–5 → John 12:41**: Isaiah "saw **his** [Jesus'] glory." The one Isaiah saw was Yahweh of hosts.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Jesus is the 'first and last' in a different sense."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"Then show me the text that makes the difference."* Same title, same book, same speaker formula.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Hebrews 1:8 should say 'God is your throne.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: v.8 opens "**to** the Son He says." The Father is speaking *to* the Son. And v.10 ("You, Lord…") has no throne issue at all.

opener.text: *"Who is the First and the Last in Isaiah 44:6?"* (They'll say Jehovah.) *"Does being the First and the Last mean you have a beginning?"* (No.)

closer.text: *"Jehovah says there's no God besides Him, and He gives His titles, His Psalm and His glory to Jesus. So either Jehovah shares His glory with a creature (Isa 42:8), or Jesus is Jehovah."*

opener.text: *"Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?"*

lead.text: → Run the full [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play). Best JW order: **Acts 13:2 → Eph 4:30 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 + Acts 4:24–25.** JW panels often go quiet at this point because they have no answer.

*"He didn't say 'I'm not good.' He asked a question to expose the man's thinking."*
*"If Jesus is good, what does that make Him?"*

defense.objection: "John 1:1 says 'a god.' No article = indefinite."
defense.response: A predicate noun before the verb without the article describes **nature** (Colwell / qualitative). "The Word was God" in nature.
defense.goTo: John 1:1; **1 John 4:8** (*ho theos agapē estin*); **John 1:6** (*para theou*, no article)
defense.askBack: *"Is God 'a love'? Was John sent from 'a god'? Your NWT says 'God' in 1:6. Why not in 1:1?"*

defense.objection: "*Ton theon* = the Almighty; *theos* = a lesser god."
defense.response: That's just Greek case. *Ton theon* is accusative after *pros*; *theos* is nominative. Case endings aren't ranks.
defense.askBack: *"Is the Father a lesser god when he's in the nominative?"*

defense.objection: "Firstborn of creation" (Col 1:15) = first created
defense.response: *Prōtotokos* = preeminent heir. v.16 gives the reason: "**because** by Him all things were created."
defense.askBack: *"Who was Israel's first king? Saul. So how is David 'firstborn' of the kings?"*

defense.objection: "Only-begotten" (John 3:16) = uniquely created
defense.response: *Monogenēs* = one-of-a-kind / unique (Heb 11:17: Isaac wasn't Abraham's only son).
defense.askBack: *"Was Isaac Abraham's only child?"*

defense.objection: "Beginning of the creation of God" (Rev 3:14)
defense.response: *Archē* = origin / ruler / source. He's where creation comes from.
defense.askBack: *"If you're the originator of your business, aren't you its origin?"*

defense.objection: "John 5:19: Jesus can do nothing on his own"
defense.response: That shows the Persons are distinct and act together. Finish the verse: "whatever the Father does, **the Son does likewise**."
defense.askBack: *"Does the Father do anything without the Son?"*

defense.objection: "John 6:57 / 14:28: 'the Father is greater'"
defense.response: Greater in role, in the Son's humbled human state. Not in nature. Phil 2:6–7.
defense.askBack: *"Is a husband 'greater' in nature than his wife because he leads?"* ➕

defense.objection: "Psalm 8 / Heb 2: everything is subject to *man*, not Jesus"
defense.response: Heb 2:9 identifies the "him": "**namely Jesus**."
defense.askBack: *"Who are we going to trust, you or the author of Hebrews?"*

defense.objection: "Daniel 7: Jesus wasn't seated / Rev 3:21: believers sit on the throne too"
defense.response: Sharing kingdom authority ≠ sitting **on high** in heaven, the place that belongs to Yahweh alone (Ps 113:5).
defense.askBack: *"Show me anyone other than Jesus who sits 'on high' at the right hand of the Majesty."*

defense.objection: "Holy Spirit = active force"
defense.response: → [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play)
defense.askBack: *"Can a force be grieved?"*

defense.objection: "Trinity isn't in the Bible."
defense.response: Word–concept fallacy. "Jehovah's Witness" isn't in the Bible as a denomination name either. Is the *concept* taught?
defense.askBack: *"Is the word 'theocracy' in the Bible?"*

beliefs.text: Yahweh = the Father alone, one person. Jesus = a human Messiah (Biblical Unitarian) or a created spirit being (Arian). No real pre-existence. Jesus is God's "agent" (*shaliach*), so whatever He says or does as God is "agency." The Spirit = God's power or presence, not a person.

lead.label: Their strength
lead.text: they've drilled the Jesus texts (agency, "the Father is the only true God," John 17:3).

lead.label: Their weak spot
lead.text: **the Holy Spirit** and the **Angel of Yahweh**. Go there early.

cheatCard.text: **Acts 13:2** → *"Do actions have authority, or do persons?"*
**Heb 3:7–11 / Ps 95** → *"Who's the 'Me' the Spirit says they tested?"*
**Gen 31:11–13** → the Angel of God says "**I am** the God of Bethel." *"Where's the 'thus says the Lord'?"*
**1 Cor 8:6 + 1 Cor 10:9 + Num 21:5–6** → *"When was Christ put to the test with serpents?"*
**John 1:3 / Col 1:16** → *"How were all things created through Him if He didn't exist yet?"*
**Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17** → *"So Yahweh has a beginning?"*

notes.text: *"You can't even answer one of three."*

opener.text: *"Does the Spirit have a mind? Yes or no?"*

lead.text: → [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play). Best order against Unitarians: **"Does the Spirit have a mind? Yes or no?"** → Acts 13:2 → Heb 3:7–11 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 / Acts 4:25 → Rom 8:9 ("Spirit of Christ").

offense.title: The Angel of Yahweh claims to be God, with no "thus says the Lord"

chain.text: **Gen 31:11–13**: "the **Angel of God** said… '**I am the God of Bethel**, where you anointed a pillar and made a vow **to me**.'"
**Gen 28:12–13**: at Bethel the one who spoke was **Yahweh**.
**Gen 35:1**: God says, "go to Bethel… make an altar there **to the God who appeared to you**." *"Why is God saying 'go meet the God you met'?"*
**Ex 3:2–6, 14**: the Angel of Yahweh in the bush → "I AM WHO I AM."
**Zech 1:12–13; Jer 50:34**: the Angel of Yahweh **intercedes to** Yahweh of hosts. *"Who is Yahweh pleading Israel's case to?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Agency: a messenger speaks in the first person for the king."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"Show me the 'thus says the Lord.'"* There isn't one. *"Without it, how do you know when a messenger is speaking for God or for himself?"* Moses talking in his tent and Jonah running away weren't oracles just because they had the "messenger" title.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Can't an ambassador speak as the king?"*
ifTheySay.youSay: **Use their analogy:** *"Can the agent of the King claim to BE the King?"* *"Yahweh can send agents, but agents can't claim to be Yahweh, or they drop dead."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"*Malak* means a lesser being, sent by a superior."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *Malak* / *angelos* names a **function**, not a nature. John the Baptist and his disciples are called *angelos* (Mark 1:2; Luke 7:24). *"Does the word itself tell you what kind of being the messenger is?"* *"If I send you with a message, am I superior to you in nature?"*

opener.text: *"Can we be honest with the text: does the Angel of God claim to be the God of Bethel? Yes or no?"*

offense.title: Christ is the Yahweh of the Exodus
offense.subtitle: 1 Cor 8:6 → 10:9

chain.text: **1 Cor 8:6**: "one Lord, **Jesus Christ**, through whom are all things"
**1 Cor 10:9**: "we must not put **Christ** to the test, as some of them did and were destroyed by serpents"
**Num 21:5–6**: they spoke against God, and **Yahweh** sent the serpents.
➕ Also: **Jude 5** (in the strongest manuscripts): "**Jesus**, who saved a people out of Egypt."

questions.text: *"When was Christ put to the test and people destroyed by serpents?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Textual variant: some manuscripts say 'the Lord'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: Fine. In this same letter, the "one Lord" **is** Jesus Christ (8:6). Either reading lands in the same place.

opener.text: *"In Numbers 21, who did Israel test, and who sent the serpents?"* (They'll say Yahweh.)

chain.text: **John 1:1–3**: *"If all things were made through Him, could He Himself have been made?"* *"It's not a leap, it's the text."*
**Col 1:16**: *"How can all things be created through Jesus if He didn't exist yet?"* If they say "it's about church offices": read "**in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible**."

**Heb 1:5–12**: the Father is speaking from v.5 on. In v.8 He calls the Son "God," and in v.10 He calls Him the Creator Lord of Ps 102. If they say "v.8 has no 'He says'," the speaker hasn't changed since v.5.
**Acts 3:15**: "the **Author of life**." *"Where does Acts 3 limit it to 'new life'?"* Make them show it, then wait.

opener.text: *"According to John 1:3, was anything made without the Word? Yes or no?"*

chain.text: "Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd and against **the man, My Associate** (*'amiti*), declares Yahweh of hosts." *'Amiti* is used in Leviticus for an equal, a fellow of the same kind. *"Why does Yahweh call the struck Shepherd His equal?"* Jesus applies this verse to Himself (Matt 26:31).

opener.text: *"In Zechariah 13:7, who is the Shepherd that gets struck?"* (Jesus says it's Him, Matt 26:31.)

defense.objection: **The syllogism:** "YHWH is the Most High; Jesus is the Son of the Most High; if Jesus is YHWH, Jesus is his own Father."
defense.response: Equivocation. You're treating "Yahweh" as naming only one person. It can name the **nature** or **any one Person**. Jesus is Yahweh by nature, not the person of the Father.
defense.goTo: Gen 19:24 (Yahweh rains fire *from* Yahweh); Judges 1:1–2 ("Judah" = man or tribe)
defense.askBack: *"Is 'Judah' a person or a tribe?"*

defense.objection: "John 17:3: the Father is 'the only true God'"
defense.response: Yes, the Father is the only true God. Trinitarians agree. "Only" excludes **false gods**, not the Son: the same John calls Jesus "the true God" (1 John 5:20).
defense.goTo: 1 John 5:20; Jude 4 ("our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ")
defense.askBack: ➕ *"Jude calls Jesus our 'only Lord.' Does that make the Father not Lord?"*

defense.objection: "1 Cor 8:6: one God, the Father"
defense.response: Same verse: "one **Lord**, Jesus Christ." Paul splits the Shema (Deut 6:4) between Father and Son. If "one God, the Father" excludes Jesus from being God, "one Lord, Jesus" excludes the Father from being Lord.
defense.askBack: ➕ *"Is the Father not Lord?"*

defense.objection: "God is not a man" (Num 23:19; Hos 11:9)
defense.response: God is not a man **by nature** (who lies or changes). The Son **took on** a human nature (John 1:14) and stayed God.
defense.askBack: *"Can the God who made human nature add it to Himself?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus died, and God can't die"
defense.response: The Person of the Son died **in His human nature**. The divine nature doesn't die. Two natures, one Person (WCF 8.2).
defense.askBack: ➕ *"Who was crucified in 1 Cor 2:8?"*

defense.objection: "*Homoousios* / Nicaea / the church invented it"
defense.response: The term is a summary of biblical teaching, not new revelation. Answer from the text, not from church history.
defense.askBack: *"Fine. Set Nicaea aside. Let's just read Rev 3:14 / John 1:3."*

defense.objection: "*Archē* (Rev 3:14) = first creature" / "Abba means source"
defense.response: *Archē* = origin / ruler / active cause. The NT is Greek, not Hebrew, and *Abba* means "Father."
defense.askBack: *"Does the software exist before you made it?"*

defense.objection: "Context limits 'Author of life' / 'all things'"
defense.response: Make them show the verse that limits it.
defense.askBack: *"Where in the chapter does it say that?"* (then wait)

defense.objection: "The Spirit is rational energy / information / a vibe"
defense.response: → [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play)
defense.askBack: *"Can energy be rational without personhood?"*

beliefs.text: The Father, Son and Holy Ghost are **three separate beings** (three gods) united in purpose, the "Godhead." The Father has a body of flesh and bone (D&C 130:22). "As man now is, God once was; as God now is, man may become" (Lorenzo Snow). Exaltation: faithful humans can become gods. Joseph Smith restored the church after a "great apostasy."
